contaminationNote: Constructed in September 2026 using live historical retrieval. Only documents published/available by 2026-03-31 are stored, but current-model memory and live-search leakage cannot be excluded. This run tests discovery mechanics and repeatability, not clean historical alpha.

lanes.purpose: Official economic/industry statistics available by the Q1 cutoff.
lanes.limitations: Focused on NBS industrial/PPI series relevant to discovered changes; not an exhaustive official-agency crawl.

lanes.purpose: Company first-party orders/backlog and operating evidence.
lanes.limitations: Focused on globally relevant suppliers surfaced by industry-wide searches; not a complete issuer crawl.

lanes.purpose: Observable prices, shortages and physical supply-demand conditions.
lanes.limitations: Uses accessible market/specialist pricing evidence; many proprietary datasets remain unavailable.

lanes.purpose: Attributed reporting for cross-border supply disruptions, shortages and trade-flow changes.
lanes.limitations: Coverage concentrated on accessible Reuters historical reporting.

lanes.purpose: Specialist semiconductor, battery and commodity supply-demand evidence.
lanes.limitations: Focused on accessible TrendForce/Argus summaries rather than all paid research.
No historical community crawl was added to this Q1 multi-source run; Q1 tests repeatability of the broader source architecture without forcing a community lane.

sourceItems.title: 1Q26 memory prices continue rising as capacity shifts to server applications
normalizedClaims: TrendForce forecast 1Q26 conventional DRAM contract prices +55-60% QoQ and NAND +33-38%, with server/HBM capacity allocation squeezing other applications.

sourceItems.title: Memory Price Outlook for 1Q26 Sharply Upgraded
normalizedClaims: TrendForce raised 1Q26 conventional DRAM forecast to +90-95% QoQ and NAND to +55-60%; PC DRAM was expected to at least double and enterprise SSD +53-58%.

sourceItems.title: AI Server Demand to Drive Memory Contract Price Increases in 2Q26
normalizedClaims: At the Q1 cutoff, TrendForce still expected 2Q26 conventional DRAM +58-63% QoQ and NAND +70-75%, with capacity continuing to shift toward server/HBM.

sourceItems.title: Intel, AMD notify customers in China of lengthy waits for CPUs
normalizedClaims: Intel warned some Chinese server customers of lead times up to six months; AMD delays were 8-10 weeks for some products; Intel server CPU prices in China rose more than 10% generally.

sourceItems.title: Intel Reportedly Warns China of CPU Shortages
normalizedClaims: TrendForce summarized the Reuters CPU shortage report; it is derivative and does not add an independent origin.

sourceItems.title: GE Vernova reports fourth quarter and full year 2025 financial results
normalizedClaims: Q4 orders were $22.2B, +65% organically; Power/Electrification backlog rose $15B sequentially; gas equipment backlog plus slot reservations grew 62→83GW; Electrification equipment backlog reached $30.5B, +53% YoY.

sourceItems.title: ABB Q4 2025 results
normalizedClaims: ABB Q4 orders rose 36% reported / 32% comparable; Electrification demand was led by very strong double-digit data-center growth and new AI-ready data-center power designs.

sourceItems.title: Energy storage boom strengthens demand outlook for beaten-down lithium
normalizedClaims: Energy storage demand was becoming a major lithium demand driver after a long glut; 2026 demand forecasts were strong but supply forecasts and sodium-ion substitution created uncertainty.

sourceItems.title: EV Cells Continue Rising in December 2025; Mild Demand Pullback Expected in 1Q26
normalizedClaims: Battery-grade lithium carbonate had risen 17% MoM to CNY103,000/t in Dec 2025; EV cells rose 2-4% and ESS cells 2-3%, while ESS restocking kept utilization high.

sourceItems.title: China lithium price soars after Zimbabwe suspends export
normalizedClaims: China lithium carbonate futures jumped after Zimbabwe suspended raw mineral and lithium concentrate exports; Zimbabwe was Africa's largest lithium producer and shipped most concentrate to China.

sourceItems.title: China lithium prices tumble as weak EV sales and Middle East war cloud demand
normalizedClaims: Lithium futures fell nearly 13% as weak EV sales and external demand uncertainty challenged the bullish storage/supply narrative; storage demand remained a supportive structural factor.

sourceItems.title: Brazil sounds alarm on fertilizers as price spike spurs cheaper alternatives
normalizedClaims: Brazil delivered urea prices rose about 35% in two weeks; some sellers suspended sales and buyers shifted toward ammonium sulfate.

sourceItems.title: War in Iran threatens fresh food-price shock across developing world
normalizedClaims: Disrupted fertilizer shipments and energy costs pushed urea prices up roughly 30-40%; fertilizer trade through Hormuz was a major physical chokepoint and no global fertilizer reserve existed.

sourceItems.title: Russia stops ammonium nitrate exports for one month amid global supply crunch
normalizedClaims: Russia, a major ammonium nitrate producer/exporter, stopped exports for a month amid global tightness and a damaged domestic production asset.

sourceItems.title: Global oil and gas shipping costs surge as Iran vows to close Strait of Hormuz
normalizedClaims: Middle East-to-China VLCC rates reached an all-time high around $423,736/day; LNG tanker rates jumped more than 40% as vessel availability tightened.

sourceItems.title: China export-control enforcement expands as firms seek clarity
normalizedClaims: China was expanding export-control enforcement manpower and compliance nationwide; exporters across multiple products faced licensing uncertainty and shipping delays.

sourceItems.title: South Korea, Germany exposed to rare earths shortage
normalizedClaims: South Korea and Germany were described as exposed to rare-earth shortages as US/Japan locked long-term supply and non-China availability remained limited.

sourceItems.title: Copper's ascent above $14,000 creates investor dilemma
normalizedClaims: LME copper hit a record $14,527.50/t in an 11% one-day rally, but the move was heavily speculative/short-covering while physical China demand was weak and inventories high.

sourceItems.title: Industrial Producer Price Indexes in January 2026
sourceItems.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
normalizedClaims: Industrial purchase prices for nonferrous metals and cables rose 16.1% YoY and 4.5% MoM in January.

sourceItems.title: Industrial Producer Price Indexes in February 2026
sourceItems.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
normalizedClaims: Industrial purchase prices for nonferrous metals and cables rose 21.3% YoY and 4.8% MoM in February; nonferrous ore mining prices rose 30.2% YoY.

sourceItems.title: 2026年1—2月份规模以上工业增加值增长6.3%
normalizedClaims: Jan-Feb industrial value added grew 6.3%; general equipment +8.9%, special equipment +8.8%, electrical machinery +8.7%, computers/communications/electronics +14.2%.

sourceItems.title: Investment in Fixed Assets from January to February 2026
sourceItems.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
normalizedClaims: Jan-Feb equipment/instrument purchases rose 11.5%; power/heat/gas/water investment +13.1%; railway/ship/aerospace equipment investment +31.1%, while private investment fell 2.6%.

eventClusters.statement: The Q4 memory shortage intensified in Q1 2026: suppliers repeatedly raised DRAM/NAND price expectations as AI/server capacity allocation crowded out PC/consumer applications, and tightness was still projected to persist into Q2.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: All three observations share one specialist origin; pricing magnitude is strong but independent first-party/company evidence is still required before company selection.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Did A-share memory suppliers retain earnings upside after the Q4 re-rating and Q1 price-upgrade expectations?

eventClusters.statement: Server CPUs became a new AI-infrastructure bottleneck in China, with Intel lead times up to six months, AMD delays of 8-10 weeks and Intel server pricing generally more than 10% higher.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: TrendForce item is derivative of Reuters; event has only one independent origin and may benefit foreign CPU vendors more directly than A-share companies.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Is there a material A-share earnings bridge through server OEMs, domestic CPU substitutes, packaging/foundry or adjacent supply rather than only thematic association?

eventClusters.statement: Long-cycle power and electrification equipment demand continued accelerating into 2026, with GE Vernova and ABB independently reporting very strong order/backlog growth led by power/grid and data-center demand.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: This was already a strong Q4 narrative; new backlog confirmation may be real but expectation saturation and A-share valuation remain central.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Did any A-share supplier acquire a newly differentiated order/valuation edge versus the peers already identified in Q4?

eventClusters.statement: Energy-storage demand revived lithium economics and battery-cell pricing, while policy/export disruptions created supply upside, but weak EV demand produced sharp commodity volatility by March.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: The March 13% futures drop and weak EV sales show that storage strength does not create a one-way lithium price thesis; miners and battery makers may have opposite sensitivities.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Which A-share companies benefit from storage volume growth without requiring persistently rising lithium input prices?

eventClusters.statement: Global nitrogen-fertilizer supply tightened abruptly in March as Hormuz disruption drove urea prices sharply higher and Russia separately stopped ammonium nitrate exports.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: The shock is partly geopolitical and may reverse quickly; high prices can cause substitution or reduced fertilizer application.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Which A-share fertilizer producers have export/energy/feedstock economics that actually improve under the shock rather than suffer higher input/logistics costs?

eventClusters.statement: Oil and LNG shipping rates spiked to extreme levels in early March as Hormuz traffic collapsed and vessel availability tightened.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Single-event geopolitical shock may be short-lived and route-specific; listed shipping exposure must be verified by vessel class/route and contract mix.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Are any A-share tanker/LNG-shipping earnings sufficiently exposed to spot rates for this to be investable rather than event beta?

eventClusters.statement: China's rare-earth export-control enforcement became more operationally restrictive while non-China buyers continued to face limited supply, extending the critical-material bottleneck.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Export controls can hurt Chinese downstream exporters as well as support upstream scarcity; policy can change quickly and direct A-share profit mapping remains difficult.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Is there an A-share producer with retained upstream pricing power rather than merely a rare-earth theme label?

eventClusters.statement: Copper futures reached a spectacular record above $14,500/t, but weak China physical demand, high inventories and speculative short-covering contradicted a clean physical-shortage interpretation.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Official China input-price inflation confirms cost pressure, not necessarily physical end-demand. Reuters explicitly reports weak physical demand/high inventories.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Should the Skill reject record-price headlines when physical confirmation is absent even if producer-input inflation is visible?

eventClusters.statement: China's Jan-Feb industrial production and equipment investment were relatively strong in several equipment/electronics categories, but the signal was broad and mixed against weak private investment and some sector declines.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Broad macro growth lacks a narrow earnings transmission and may reflect state-led capex rather than listed-company expectation gaps.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Is any specific sub-industry change sufficiently differentiated to deserve a separate event, or should this remain macro context?
